name: X-Guard Control
description: Use X-guard (both legs controlling one of their legs from underneath) to off-balance and sweep the opponent to top position.
shortInstruction: Both legs on one leg, foot on their hip, off-balance and sweep — X-guard is the king of sweeps.
summary: X-guard is the most powerful sweeping position in no-gi. Both of your legs control their near leg (one hooked behind the knee, one on the hip), while you sit under their center of mass. From here, you have a 2-on-1 on their leg and control of their base. Any weight shift they make can be exploited into a sweep. X-guard is the destination of the DLR-to-X and SLX-to-X transitions.
whyItWorks: Two legs on one leg gives you an overwhelming mechanical advantage — they cannot simply pull free.
Your position under their center of mass means they have no base directly over you — they are always off-balance.
The foot on their far hip controls their rotation and prevents them from stepping away.
Danaher principle: X-guard is a 'sweep with certainty' — the position is so dominant that the sweep is almost inevitable.
commonMistakes: Letting both legs drop to the same side of their leg — one leg must hook behind, one foot on the hip.
Sitting too far from their base — your hips should be directly under their hips.
Pulling the sweep without controlling their far arm — they will post and recover.
Staying in X-guard too long — it is a transitional position; sweep or transition immediately.
coachingCues: One behind, one on top — that's X-guard.
Hips under hips, sweep with certainty.
If they post, you sweep — if they don't, they fall.
X-guard is a moment, not a home.
safetySummary: Keep your head off the mat to avoid guillotine counters when you sweep.
Do not let them stack you by driving forward — if they stack, release the X-guard and reset.
When you sweep and come on top, protect your own head from hitting the mat.
keyCorrections: If you can't sweep them, your hips are not deep enough — scoot closer so your hips are under theirs.
If they step out, your foot on the far hip lost connection — re-establish the hip post immediately.
If they grab your head, you lost the arm fight — swim your hand inside and pummel.

systemLogic.corePrinciple: Enter X-guard (one leg behind their knee, one foot on far hip) → hips under their hips → off-balance → sweep or transition.

decisionTree.action: keep pulling until they post → sweep the opposite direction.
extend into SLX or leg entanglement.

moneyDetails: Your behind-the-knee hook must be deep — foot should hook their inner thigh, not just behind the knee.
The foot on their far hip should be on the hip bone, actively pressing to control their distance.
Grab their far ankle or sleeve with your same-side hand to prevent them from stepping back.
The X-guard sweep works by pulling their hooked leg toward your chest while pushing with the hip foot — a scissoring motion.
nextStep: After X-guard control, learn the X-guard to SLX transition and the X-guard sweep variations.
fixItFast: Can't sweep? Your hips aren't under theirs — scoot closer.
They step out? Your hip foot needs more active pressure — dig it into the hip bone.
They stack you? Release the X-guard and fall to your back — don't fight the stack.
